approved: Wine and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change wine industry laws to put into action the government's response to a review of wine and grape regulations.

It would give the wine industry body new powers to run surveys, set up rules for handling information, and make clear the law's goals include supporting consumer protection rules and a planned code for wine grape buying.
The bill would also let an agricultural research agency share contact details of levy payers with a mailing company to send out survey materials, while keeping privacy safeguards.
It would let the wine industry body organise surveys of grape or wine producers.
It would create a modern framework for managing information, with protections for sensitive data.
It would update the purposes of the wine law to mention supporting consumer protection and a proposed code of conduct.
It would allow the agricultural research agency to use and share levy information, including personal details, for its work.
It would make small fixes to the rule-making power of the department's secretary.
The wine and grape industry, levy payers, and the agricultural research agency are affected.

Declared that specified telecommunications, therapeutic goods, biosecurity, and wine legislation would stand referred to the Federation Chamber, either immediately or following adjournment of second-reading debates, unless otherwise ordered.

Supported the Wine and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2026, describing its information-sharing and administrative changes as cost-neutral and groundwork for a mandatory wine industry code. Argued that the bill would not resolve structural oversupply, falling consumption and growers' financial distress, and called for a coordinated, industry-consulted transition plan, including support for voluntary exits.

Supported the Wine and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2026, arguing that it would strengthen protections for grape growers by supporting a mandatory code, improving Wine Australia surveys and enabling targeted agricultural survey mailings. Reported government support for the bill and opposition to a second reading amendment concerning volumetric alcohol taxation.
